chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Al-Ḥasan ibn Ṣāliḥ from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The Muslim bars the disbeliever and inherits from him, while the disbeliever does not bar the believer and does not inherit from him.”

key_terms.الْكَافِرَ: the disbeliever; a non-Muslim in the context of inheritance law
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنَ: the believer; here, the Muslim heir who is not excluded by a disbeliever
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمُ: the Muslim; the party whose legal status is being defined in inheritance
key_terms.يَحْجُبُ: bars or excludes another heir from inheritance

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance between a Muslim and a disbeliever in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling in inheritance between people of different religions. It establishes that a Muslim may inherit from a disbeliever and exclude him, while a disbeliever neither excludes a believer from inheritance nor inherits from him.
